title: AWS Organizations: organisational units and consolidated billing

videos.script: Six accounts are six bills, six root users and six sets of rules, unless something holds them together. {{six}} That something is AWS Organizations. One account creates an organisation and becomes its management account. Every other account joins it as a member. {{org}} The members hang from a root, in folders called organisational units. You choose the folders. The shop uses three of them: one for security, one for workloads, and a sandbox. {{tree}} In this lesson you build that tree in your lab, account by account, and move each account into its place. {{moves}} The tree matters for two reasons. The first is the bill. The whole organisation gets one, and the management account pays it. Before it applies its volume prices, AWS adds up the usage of every account. {{bill}} So two accounts that each send eight terabytes a month pay less together than apart. You will work out by how much, straight from the price list. {{tiers}} The second reason is rules, which the next lesson attaches to the branches of the tree. {{rules}} And then a warning. The management account can reach into every member, and no rule of the organisation reaches it. So it runs nothing at all. {{end}}
